description: Server-side PKI work: the local gateway still runs on a SHA-1 legacy CA. Build a new SHA-256 CA in pki/current/, re-issue the server certificate from the same CSR, publish a legacy CRL revoking the old serial, switch proxy/gw.conf to the new files and write report/migration.md with eight keys; checks.py recomputes all eight with openssl and runs verify.sh, and the live server keeps serving TLS on the new chain. Needs openssl on PATH and in the run's --auto-approve (not in the default set).

criteria: The agent built a new SHA-256 CA in pki/current/, re-issued the server certificate from the same CSR with a fresh serial, published pki/legacy/crl.pem revoking the old serial under the legacy CA, and switched proxy/gw.conf to the new files, leaving the verify.sh gate, the checks, the incident note, the legacy CA/CSR and the server key untouched.

python3 checks.py passes: all eight report keys match the openssl-recomputed values and bash verify.sh exits 0 (new chain verifies for sslserver, old cert fails against the new anchor and fails -crl_check against the legacy CRL).
